subtitle: The Baoli of Goindval and the Steps of Equality

panels.shot: low-angle wide of riverside town with monumental stepped well at dawn
panels.action: Guru Amar Das stands beside the newly built 84-step baoli at Goindval, his aged yet steady figure framed against the pale sky as villagers of all kinds descend the broad steps toward the shimmering water.

dialogue.text: In Goindval on the Beas, Guru Amar Das, Third Guru of the Sikhs, carves into earth and custom a living stairway toward equality.

i18n.hi: ब्यास किनारे गोइंदवाल में, गुरु अमर दास, तीसरे सिख गुरु, मिट्टी और रिवाज़ में बराबरी की जिंदा सीढ़ियाँ गढ़ते हैं।

panels.shot: medium-wide of dusty Punjab road, following behind a bent old man carrying a water pot
panels.action: A younger but still grey-bearded Amar Das walks along a sun-baked path with a brass water pot on his shoulder, his simple clothes dusty, his gaze turned toward the distant village where Guru Angad dwells.

dialogue.text: Before he was Guru, Amar Das walked the hot paths of Punjab, an old man with a burning thirst for the Name, bringing water each dawn to Guru Angad at Khadoor.

i18n.hi: गुरु बनने से पहले, अमर दास तपते पंजाब में नंगे पाँव चलते, नाम की प्यास से जलता बूढ़ा, हर सुबह खडूर में गुरु अंगद को पानी पहुँचा आता।

panels.shot: intimate interior medium shot, candlelit, Amar Das seated at Guru Angad's feet (Guru off-frame implied)
panels.action: Inside a modest village hut lit by a single lamp, Amar Das sits low on the floor, head bowed, hands folded, listening with wet eyes as an unseen voice recites the hymns of Nanak and Angad.

dialogue.text: He was in his seventies when he found Guru Angad, and in that humble house he drank the shabad, the Word, until his heart belonged wholly to seva.

i18n.hi: सत्तर पार में उन्हें गुरु अंगद मिले, और उस सादे घर में उन्होंने शब्द का रस पीया, जब तक दिल पूरी तरह सेवा का हो न गया।

panels.shot: dramatic interior wide, low-angle on Amar Das as he is addressed, others around him bowing
panels.action: In a larger hall at Khadoor, elders and disciples sit in a circle as Amar Das, frail yet radiant, rises slightly from his seat while others bow; the sense is of anointment, though Guru Angad is only suggested beyond frame.

dialogue.text: In 1552, Guru Angad passed the mantle to the servant who never tired, Amar Das of Basarke, making the old sevadar the Third Guru of the Sikhs.

i18n.hi: १५५२ में, गुरु अंगद ने कभी न थकने वाले सेवक, बसरके के अमर दास पर गद्दी सौंपी, और बुज़ुर्ग सेवक तीसरे सिख गुरु बने।

panels.shot: bird's-eye wide of Goindval under construction on the Beas riverbank
panels.action: From above, tents, half-built houses, and channels being dug spread around the curve of the Beas; Guru Amar Das stands amid workers, pointing toward the center where a great square pit is being marked out.

dialogue.text: He turned his face to Goindval on the Beas, a new center on an old road, and began to shape more than a town: a place where water, work and worship would flow together.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने रुख ब्यास किनारे गोइंदवाल की ओर किया, पुरानी राह पर नया टिकाण, और बस नगर नहीं, ऐसी धरती गढ़नी शुरू की जहाँ पानी, मेहनत और इबादत एक साथ बहें।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of baoli excavation with workers and baskets of earth
panels.action: Men and women together haul baskets of soil from a deep, squared excavation; Guru Amar Das stands at the edge, bare feet in dust, hands raised in blessing as the stepped form of the baoli slowly appears.

dialogue.text: At its heart he set a baoli, a stepped well of eighty-four steps, dug by the hands of farmers and traders, of women and men, to hold the river’s gift in common.

i18n.hi: बीचोंबीच उन्होंने एक बावली रखी—चौरासी सीढ़ियों का कुआँ, जिसे किसानों–व्यापारियों, औरत–मर्द, सबके हाथों ने खोदा, ताकि नदी का तोहफा सबका हो।

panels.shot: medium shot at mid-level of baoli, showing varied people on steps
panels.action: Inside the completed baoli, villagers in different clothes descend the long flights of stone: a veiled woman, a leatherworker, a trader in fine cloth, a farmer; Guru Amar Das watches from a mid-landing with a gentle smile.

dialogue.text: Here the Guru broke subtle walls: all feet touched the same stone, all hands dipped into the same water; caste and rank lost their sharp edge on the cool steps.

i18n.hi: यहीं गुरु ने अदृश्य दीवारें तोड़ीं: सबके पाँव एक ही पत्थर से लगे, सबके हाथ एक ही पानी में डूबे; जात–पात, ओहदा सबकी धार ठंडी सीढ़ियों पर कुंद हो गई।

panels.shot: interior wide of langar hall with long rows of seated diners
panels.action: In a spacious hall lined with reed mats, people of many backgrounds sit in straight rows eating simple food while Guru Amar Das moves slowly along the line, overseeing the serving with serene attention.

dialogue.text: Beside the baoli, he strengthened another river: the langar, where hungry bodies met hot roti, and where the high sat low, shoulder to shoulder with the poor.

i18n.hi: बावली के साथ उन्होंने दूसरी नदी भी मज़बूत की—लंगर, जहाँ भूखी देह को गरम रोटी मिली, और ऊँचे लोग नीचे बैठकर ग़रीबों के कंधे से कंधा मिला कर खाने लगे।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Amar Das serving food to a wealthy-looking man
panels.action: Guru Amar Das kneels to place a coarse bread and lentils before a richly dressed visitor who looks uneasy to be seated amid laborers and women, his jewelry catching the firelight.

dialogue.speaker: guru_amar_das
dialogue.text: First sit and eat as one; only then may you speak of God.

i18n.hi: पहले एक साथ बैठकर खाओ, फिर भगवान की बात करो।

panels.shot: dim interior, focused medium shot on Amar Das reciting to a small group of scribes
panels.action: By lamplight in a quiet room, Guru Amar Das sits before low desks where attentive scribes write on paper; he chants verses, fingers gently tapping time, while manuscripts lie stacked nearby.

dialogue.text: As Goindval grew in brick and stone, he also built in ink and sound, teaching and compiling hymns that would later flow into the Guru Granth, weaving devotion with a stern eye on injustice.

i18n.hi: जैसे गोइंदवाल ईंट–पत्थर से बढ़ा, वैसे ही उन्होंने स्याही और सुर से भी इमारत उठाई; शिक्षाएँ दीं, शबद जोड़े, जो आगे चलकर गुरु ग्रंथ में बहेंगे, भक्ति को ज़ुल्म के ख़िलाफ़ सख़्त नज़र से बुनते हुए।

panels.shot: intimate interior medium shot with Amar Das addressing a group of women, some veiled
panels.action: In a sunlit courtyard, several women sit before Guru Amar Das; some keep their veils drawn, others let them fall back as he speaks, his hand lightly raised in a gesture of reassurance.

dialogue.text: He saw how women were hidden behind veils and walls, their voices folded away, and he spoke openly that the soul has no gender, that a wife and husband both walk the path.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने देखा कैसे औरतें परदे–दीवारों के पीछे क़ैद हैं, उनकी आवाज़ें दबा दी गईं; उन्होंने साफ़ कहा कि आत्मा का कोई लिंग नहीं, कि पति–पत्नी दोनों रास्ता साथ चलते हैं।

panels.shot: somber interior wide, with Amar Das between a grieving widow and an elder urging her toward a pyre off-frame
panels.action: In a shaded room, a young widow sits pale and rigid, bangles broken, while an elder points insistently toward the courtyard beyond where a smoky pyre is visible; Guru Amar Das steps between them, his face firm.

dialogue.text: In his hymns he struck at sati, the burning of widows, saying the true sati is she who lives in remembrance, who keeps faith in life, not in a husband’s funeral fire.

i18n.hi: अपने शबदों में उन्होंने सती की आग पर चोट की, कहा सच्ची सती वही जो याद में जीती है, जो ज़िंदगी में विश्वास रखती है, न कि पति की चिता की लपटों में।

panels.shot: medium close-up on the widow’s face as Amar Das speaks gently beside her
panels.action: Close on the widow’s tear-streaked face as she looks uncertainly at Guru Amar Das seated beside her, his palm open toward her as if holding out a different future.

dialogue.speaker: guru_amar_das
dialogue.text: Your courage is not in dying on fire, daughter, but in living in truth.

i18n.hi: तेरी बहादुरी आग में मरने में नहीं, बेटी, सच में जीने में है।

panels.shot: exterior wide of a congregation where a woman stands addressing listeners with Amar Das watching
panels.action: In the open ground near Goindval, a woman stands upon a raised platform, speaking to a mixed crowd; Guru Amar Das watches from the side, approving, as men and women alike listen.

dialogue.text: He did not keep women as mere listeners; he entrusted them with piri seats, alongside the manjis, to teach and organize, so that guidance flowed through both daughters and sons of the Panth.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने औरतों को सिर्फ़ सुनने वाली नहीं छोड़ा; उन्हें पीरी की सीटें दीं, मंजियों के साथ, सिखाने और संगठित करने को, ताकि रहनुमाई पंथ की बेटियों–बेटों दोनों से बहे।

panels.shot: map-like overhead with small vignettes of different manjis, Amar Das in foreground dispatching a follower
panels.action: In the foreground, Guru Amar Das hands a staff and cloth to a devoted Sikh before a simple map of Punjab, where small scenes show teachers sitting with sangats in distant villages.

dialogue.text: Through twenty-two manjis he stretched the fabric of the community across the land, each seat a small school of equality, funded by the dasvandh, the tenth share offered by willing hearts.

i18n.hi: बाइस मंजियों से उन्होंने संगत की चादर पूरे देस पर तानी, हर मंजा बराबरी का छोटा विद्यालय, जो चलती थी दसवंध से—दिल से दी गई कमाई की दसवीं हिस्सेदारी से।

panels.shot: busy langar hall wide, with a notable noble or courtly figure seated inconspicuously in the row
panels.action: In a crowded langar, amid farmers and artisans, a dignified man in fine Mughal-style garments sits cross-legged, his jewelry subdued; Guru Amar Das walks past with a serving bowl, treating him no differently from the rest.

dialogue.text: Tradition tells how even men close to throne and court sat in his langar, their silk meeting the rough cotton of peasants, their titles set aside as food and humility were shared.

i18n.hi: रिवायत कहती है कि दरबारों–तख़्तों के करीब बैठे मर्द भी उसके लंगर में बैठे, उनकी रेशम की पोशाकें किसानों के खुरदरे सूत से घिसीं, और ओहदे उतार कर सबने रोटी और नम्रता बाँटी।

panels.shot: evening interior medium shot, Amar Das instructing the young Ram Das
panels.action: In the soft light of evening, Guru Amar Das sits facing a younger disciple, Ram Das, speaking earnestly; scrolls and a rough plan of Goindval lie between them, while voices of the langar drift faintly.

dialogue.text: In his later years he prepared succession with care, training Ram Das to carry forward not only song and prayer, but the institutions of langar, dasvandh, manjis and the living example of Goindval.

i18n.hi: बुढ़ापे में उन्होंने उत्तराधिकार भी संभाल कर सजाया, राम दास को सिर्फ़ कीर्तन–अरदास नहीं, बल्कि लंगर, दसवंध, मंजियों और गोइंदवाल की ज़िंदा मिसाल के संस्थान सौंपने की तालीम दी।

panels.shot: twilight wide of baoli and langar, Amar Das walking slowly among people of all kinds
panels.action: At twilight, lamps glow around the baoli and langar as Guru Amar Das walks slowly through the mingling crowd—widows chatting, women leaders, traders, laborers—his hand brushing the stone railing of the steps.

dialogue.text: In Goindval the Guru showed that equality is not only a word in a hymn; it is a staircase, a kitchen, a seat of teaching, repeated in daily discipline until custom itself begins to change.

i18n.hi: गोइंदवाल में गुरु ने दिखाया कि बराबरी सिर्फ़ भजन की पंक्ति नहीं; वो सीढ़ियाँ हैं, रसोई है, शिक्षा का आसन है, जो रोज़ की सख़्त रियाज़ में दोहराए जाते हैं, जब तक रिवाज़ खुद बदलना शुरू न कर दे।

panels.shot: final reflective shot, close on Amar Das’s serene face with baoli steps blurred behind
panels.action: Guru Amar Das sits near the top of the baoli, eyes half closed in quiet joy, as the long line of steps stretches behind him into soft focus, filled with faint figures going up and down.

dialogue.text: Long after his passing in 1574, the steps he cut into earth and habit remain: water for all, food for all, a path where the Guru’s word on equality still echoes under every shared meal.

i18n.hi: १५७४ में उनके जाने के बहुत बाद भी, मिट्टी और आदत में काटी गई वो सीढ़ियाँ आज तक हैं: सबके लिए पानी, सबके लिए खाना, वो राह जहाँ गुरु का बराबरी वाला शब्द हर साझा निवाले के नीचे अब भी गूँजता है।
